title: Break Reference Cycles
goal: Prevent memory leaks in shared data structures using Weak pointers.

sections.text: Two `Rc` pointers referring to each other create a reference cycle. Their reference counts never hit zero, so their allocated heap memory is leaked forever.
A `Weak<T>` pointer holds a reference to data managed by `Rc` without incrementing the strong reference count.

sections.caption: Rc::downgrade creates a non-owning weak handle.

sections.text: Because a `Weak<T>` handle does not own the data, the inner value might be dropped at any time when all strong `Rc` handles go away.
You cannot dereference a `Weak<T>` directly. You must call `.upgrade()`, which returns an `Option<Rc<T>>`.

sections.caption: upgrade returns None if the inner value was already dropped.

explanation: Prevent memory leaks in shared data structures using Weak pointers.
